commitResults.messageTitle: Add ClientHistoryFormatter for the view command (#78)
commitResults.messageBody:
Build the text for one client's details and full measurement and
performance history in a non-UI class so it can be unit-tested.
Records are listed newest first. Same-date measurements follow the
type order weight, bodyfat, waist; same-date performances are shown
most recently recorded first so the first line matches the card's
"Latest performance".

Move PhoneDisplayFormatter from ui to commons.util so Logic does not
depend on UI; PersonCard only changes its import.

AI-assisted: Claude Code drafted parts of this change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add view command to show a client's full history (#78)
commitResults.messageBody:
"view INDEX" shows the client at the displayed index in the result
display, using ClientHistoryFormatter. Parsing follows delete: a
missing, non-numeric or extra argument is a format error, while 0, a
negative number or an out-of-range index is an invalid index.

The command is read-only, so the data and the displayed list are
unchanged and LogicManager does not save.

AI-assisted: Claude Code drafted parts of this change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for data files with invalid values (#79)
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file that is valid JSON but breaks a model constraint (invalid
phone or email, out-of-range or unknown measurement, duplicate
measurement, invalid performance sets/reps/load) should start Spotter
with no clients, record the load warning, and leave the file unchanged.

Each file also contains a valid client so that a partial load would be
detected, and a control test checks the same layout loads normally.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support email removal in EditPersonDescriptor
commitResults.messageBody:
A client's email is optional, but an edit could only keep or replace
it. The descriptor now distinguishes an unchanged email from one that
should be removed, so EditCommand can clear the email while keeping
the client's other details and records.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove email when edit is given an empty e/
commitResults.messageBody:
Trainers had no way to clear an outdated email. An empty e/ now
removes it, matching how an empty t/ clears tags. Invalid and
repeated email values are still rejected as before.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document email removal in the edit command
Cover all records in email removal test
commitResults.messageBody:
The email removal test only gave the client a session, so dropping
the measurement or performance history would still have passed. The
client now has all three, and the shared measurement is a constant.

commitResults.messageTitle: Track email removal with a flag in the descriptor
commitResults.messageBody:
Reviewers found Optional<Optional<Email>> hard to read, and Optional
fields are discouraged. EditPersonDescriptor now keeps a plain Email
with an isEmailRemoved flag, so getEmail() returns Optional<Email>
again. setEmail and removeEmail each reset the other, so the two
states cannot conflict.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that copying a descriptor keeps email removal
commitResults.messageBody:
The copy constructor must carry isEmailRemoved over, or an
EditCommand would silently keep the email it was asked to remove.
The test compares a copied removal descriptor with its original.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertion and logging to EditCommand
commitResults.messageBody:
An edit must never both replace and remove a client's email. The
descriptor's setters keep this true, so EditCommand now asserts it
before building the edited client. Successful edits are also logged
by index, without client details, to help trace user actions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a list of upcoming sessions to Model
commitResults.messageBody:
The Upcoming sessions panel needs every client with a booked session,
soonest first, whatever the current find or filter. Build the list from
the whole address book, reusing PersonSessionComparator and the client
card's rule for an upcoming session, and refresh it before each command
so that sessions that have passed drop off.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show upcoming sessions beside the client list
commitResults.messageBody:
Trainers need to see who is next and prepare for them at a glance.
Split the window so that the client list stays on the left and the
right shows one card per upcoming session, soonest first, with the
client's phone and latest records. The cards reuse the client card's
formatters and have no index, so they cannot be mistaken for the
client list's indices.

Lower the window's minimum height so that it fits 1280x720 at 150%.

commitResults.messageTitle: Track the client shown by view in Model
commitResults.messageBody:
To show a client's history in the side panel and keep it current while
records are logged, the model must know which client is viewed. Hold
it in an observable property, and follow the client through setPerson,
since Person is immutable. Stop viewing a client that is deleted or no
longer in a replaced address book.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show view's client history in the side panel
commitResults.messageBody:
The result display is only a few lines tall and is replaced by the next
command's result, so a long history was hard to read and went stale as
soon as a record was logged. Show it in the side panel instead, in
place of Upcoming sessions, and keep it in sync with the viewed client.
The result display now only confirms which client is shown.

list, deleting that client, or clear bring Upcoming sessions back. If
saving fails, the viewed client is restored with the rest of the data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name: normalize equivalent accent encodings
commitResults.messageBody:
Equivalent accented names are treated as different clients when one is
written with a precomposed character and the other with a combining
mark (for example, "José" versus "Jose" plus U+0301).

The two forms spell the same name but produce different strings, so
duplicate detection, full-name lookup and keyword search distinguish
them despite them being the same client.

Let's normalize names to Unicode NFC before validation, storage and
lookup, and normalize search keywords the same way.

NFC preserves accents and scripts instead of transliterating them, so
"José" and "Jose" without the accent remain different names while the
two encodings of one spelling become one identity.

TextField discards tabs before command parsing, joining neighbouring
arguments. Normalize tabs to spaces before the control filters them.
Exercise direct input and real clipboard paste, selection and undo.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject arguments before clearing client data
commitResults.messageBody:
An accidental clear 1 removes every client. Reject nonblank arguments
before executing the destructive command, while accepting whitespace.
Verify rejected commands preserve clients, filters, history and JSON.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test Help restoration without a window manager
commitResults.messageBody: Xvfb does not minimize shown windows without a desktop window manager. Assert the iconified-state reset before showing the stage, and retain a shown-window restoration check without assuming native minimization is available.

commitResults.messageTitle: Isolate Help tests from native window callbacks
commitResults.messageBody:
A shown Linux stage reports iconified state asynchronously. Keep the
unconditional regression on a hidden stage and test shown-stage focus
separately, without assuming a window manager responds synchronously.

commitResults.messageTitle: Build the clear usage error from its command word
commitResults.messageBody:
The extra-parameter message repeats the command name as literals.
Reuse COMMAND_WORD in both places, matching ListCommand while keeping
the displayed error text unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Number the Help restoration manual checks
commitResults.messageBody:
The Help restoration instructions sit outside the surrounding numbered
manual-test cases. Group them into a numbered case after launch and
window preferences, with separate command and menu/shortcut checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove the trailing break from tab guidance
commitResults.messageBody:
The pasted-tabs bullet has no continuation line. Remove its trailing
HTML break so it uses the same spacing as the other single-line items.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify parentheses in exercise labels
commitResults.messageBody:
Exercise labels treat parentheses as literal characters, without a
balancing restriction. Document this decision and test unmatched opening
and closing parentheses. Rename the constructor test to match the
project convention requested in review.

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn when cancellation changes displayed indices
commitResults.messageBody: Compare the cancelled client's position before and after updating the model so full-list reordering also produces a warning. Avoid claiming lower rows moved when the last filtered row disappears, and share client resolution with booking.

commitResults.messageTitle: Simplify session parsing and reuse display helpers
commitResults.messageBody: Keep the two client identifiers separate while sharing date and time parsing. Construct the comparator chain once per sort and cache immutable card formatters without changing date rules or ordering.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document cancellation warnings for changed indices
commitResults.messageBody: Explain warnings for both client removal from a filtered view and reordering into the unbooked group. Describe the shared booking and cancellation resolver.

commitResults.messageBody: The e7ed72b7 revert-of-revert restored session files byte for byte after 8ac2965a, causing blame to credit the restorer. Trace the affected blocks to Gabriel's earlier commits and annotate their genuine authorship for RepoSense without rewriting history. Leave later teammate feature implementations outside these blocks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep session times explicitly formatted to minutes
commitResults.messageBody: Retain the HH:mm formatter requested during review and check midnight and single-digit-hour command forms end to end. Stored next-session values keep their documented minute precision.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept valid hyphenated email domains
commitResults.messageBody:
Email validation repeated a whole label to enforce a two-character
minimum, rejecting valid short hyphenated labels. Validate label
endpoints directly and cover add, edit and stored-data round trips.

commitResults.messageTitle: Sort displayed tags without case bias
commitResults.messageBody:
Mixed-case tags appeared in character-code order in both client views.
Share a deterministic alphabetical comparator and verify the formatter
and actual JavaFX card/detail output.

Refs #198

commitResults.messageTitle: Sort accented client names alphabetically
commitResults.messageBody:
Accepted Latin names with accents sorted after Z. Use explicit English
collation for client ordering and booking-clash feedback while keeping
identity comparisons unchanged. Verify each session group and warning.

Refs #197

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the positive integer overflow boundary
commitResults.messageBody:
Integer.MAX_VALUE + 1 overflowed before conversion, so two tests
exercised a negative number. Calculate in long arithmetic and also
check that the largest valid positive integer remains accepted.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify record dates and repair guide navigation

between future-date command validation and stored-record recovery.
Repair the shared DG sidebar link to its current rendered heading.

commitResults.messageTitle: Run OS checks one at a time
commitResults.messageBody:
Limit each matrix run to one concurrent OS job to reduce runner bursts.
Keep all platforms, build commands and existing failure behaviour.
This is a mitigation suggested in course forum #728, not a guarantee
that GitHub will stop disabling workflows.
